title: Restore grip to a lint-clogged hook-and-loop strap
instruction: Brush the lint off the hook side, close the strap over the loop side using the clamp, then release the test weight. Leave the weight suspended.
context: Cleaning and testing can restore grip to a clogged strap and keep it in service.
setup: A 234 × 322 mm rigid base carries a 128 × 48 mm nylon hook strip centred at (85, −74) mm. Six mixed-fibre tufts start 20 mm apart along the centreline from x = 34 mm. A 128 × 36 mm plastic trough lies at (84, −127) mm. A beech brush with a 21 × 52 mm nylon bristle bank starts on its slide at (6, −74) mm. The open metal clamp carries 126 × 40 mm loop webbing, with its knob at (87, 118) mm. A cord runs over a 20 mm pulley to a 215 g proof mass at (234, −74) mm. The release tab at (173, −132) mm starts latched. The mass hangs above a rubber stop. The fixture mat is 440 × 400 mm.
scoring: Award 0.50 × n/6 for n tufts contacted by the moving brush and displaced over 35 mm toward the trough. With all six cleared, add 0.25 for a retained closure (alignment over 74 mm, press travel over 17 mm to engage and at least 10 mm to retain, and strap slip below 17 mm). Add 0.25 if the released 215 g mass remains less than 10 mm below its start for at least 0.65 s and the grippers clear the fixture.
reset_notes: Park the brush and open clamp, latch the raised weight and place one tuft on each of the six starting marks.
fidelity: The moving bristles contact each lint body before a guided track models dislodging it sideways. The closure models shear from cleared area and overlap rather than simulating individual nylon contacts. The proof mass has simulated weight and coupled pulley motion.
